brief: Non-profit working to end the killing of dogs and cats in shelters. We're looking for monthly donors, ideally pet owners who care about adoption. Would a donation ask work at checkout?

profile.business_summary: A non-profit organization dedicated to ending the killing of dogs and cats in shelters, seeking to acquire monthly recurring donors at checkout.
profile.product: Monthly donation subscription to support animal shelter rescue and adoption efforts.
stated_claims: Working to end the killing of dogs and cats in shelters.

relevant_tags.why: The core target audience is pet owners who care about animal welfare and adoption.
Shoppers buying pet supplies are pet owners and highly likely to care about pet welfare.
Shoppers buying pet food are pet owners and highly likely to care about pet welfare.
The advertiser is specifically looking for monthly recurring donors.

note_signals.why: Pet subscription brand with health-conscious owners, highly aligned with pet adoption and welfare.
Largest pet audience in the catalog, ideal for reaching a broad base of pet owners.
Millennials treating dogs as family, highly receptive to pet welfare causes.
Audience responds well to social-good messaging, making them prime candidates for donation asks.

profile.gate_reason: The non-profit's goal of securing monthly donors from pet owners is clear, and we have several highly aligned pet and social-good publishers to test this checkout donation ask.
clarifying_questions: What are your target monthly donation amounts (e.g., $10, $25, $50)?
Do you accept one-time donations at checkout, or only monthly recurring subscriptions?
Are your operations and donor tax-deductibility limited to a specific country (e.g., US only)?

config.advertiser_summary: A non-profit organization dedicated to ending the killing of dogs and cats in shelters, seeking to acquire monthly recurring donors at checkout.

assumptions: Price not given; assumed $60 for a 'unknown' product.
subscription: assumed 4.0 orders per customer over ~6 months.
No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 45% gross margin (typical for pet). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($60 x 45% margin x 4.0 orders = $108.00).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $75.60 x click-to-purchase rate (1.1%-3.9% for pet). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.36 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.33 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.36 -> relative fit x1.39 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.32 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.33 -> relative fit x1.32 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.20 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $2,420, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $75.60 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
